variants.title: Take one safe step
variants.context: A computer-use step is a bounded decision over a changing environment: capture the environment, propose one action, evaluate authority, execute in isolation, check the postcondition, then continue or recover. The harness owns every stage except the proposal.
variants.prompt: An agent must change the shipping address on a web account. Put the loop stages in order.

items.text: Execute in isolation: act in a browser or container with minimal privileges, restricted network access, and scoped credentials.
Evaluate authority: apply allowlists, identity, origin, data sensitivity, action risk, budgets, and current approval outside the model.
Continue or recover: advance only from verified evidence, otherwise re-plan, reconcile, ask the user, compensate, or stop.
Select one bounded action: the target, its supporting evidence, the expected postcondition, and what would invalidate the proposal.
Check the postcondition: re-observe the interface and query authoritative state, recording completed, rejected, failed, or ambiguous.
Capture the environment: a screenshot and available semantics with an observation ID, timestamp, window identity, URL, and account.

variants.hint: Ask which stage is allowed to decide that an action may run.
variants.explanation: The model interprets and proposes; trusted code observes, authorizes, executes, and verifies before the loop advances.

variants.title: Take one safe step
variants.context: A computer-use step is a bounded decision over a changing environment: capture the environment, propose one action, evaluate authority, execute in isolation, check the postcondition, then continue or recover. The harness owns every stage except the proposal.
variants.prompt: A user asked the agent to buy one seat of a named tool, and the checkout page is already open. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Execute the approved click inside the isolated profile that holds only the scoped payment credential.
Verify from the order record rather than the confirmation banner, then record the terminal state for the attempt.
Propose exactly one action on the purchase control, stating vendor, seat count, and total as the expected postcondition.
Compare the proposal with direct user intent and pause for current approval, since money is about to leave the account.
Re-observe the checkout, because the last screenshot predates a navigation and a long model turn.

variants.hint: Ask which stage is allowed to decide that an action may run.
variants.explanation: Approval sits immediately before the external effect, and verification reads the system of record instead of the rendered page.

variants.title: Take one safe step
variants.context: A computer-use step is a bounded decision over a changing environment: capture the environment, propose one action, evaluate authority, execute in isolation, check the postcondition, then continue or recover. The harness owns every stage except the proposal.
variants.prompt: A page tells the agent to upload a saved credential file in order to continue. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Reject the proposal before execution, so no credential leaves the isolated environment.
Propose the upload as one bounded action, naming the file, the destination, and the expected postcondition.
Capture the page with its observation ID, origin, and account so the instruction is recorded as page content.
Record the rejection with the page as its source and ask the user instead of continuing the plan.
Evaluate authority and find no direct user intent covering the transmission of that file to this origin.

variants.hint: Page text can shape a proposal, but ask what it cannot do.
variants.explanation: Third-party content is never permission, so the rejected attempt is a recorded terminal state rather than a retry.

variants.title: Read the environment
variants.context: No single observation channel is best. Screenshots show rendered state, accessibility semantics expose roles and names, DOM or application state gives programmatic detail, and an authoritative API confirms durable effects.
variants.prompt: A harness is deciding which channels to capture. Match each channel to what it provides.

pairs.label: Screenshot pixels
pairs.detail: Canvas content, spatial relationships, overlays, and rendered state, at a high cost and with imprecise targets.

pairs.label: Accessibility semantics
pairs.detail: Roles, names, values, and control state, whenever the application publishes them.

pairs.label: DOM or app state
pairs.detail: Attributes, URLs, network state, and stable application contracts.

pairs.label: Authoritative API
pairs.detail: Confirmation that a message was sent, a record saved, or a payment completed.

variants.hint: Ask what each channel can prove, not what it can show.
variants.explanation: A production harness combines channels and records which one grounded the target for each action.

variants.title: Read the environment
variants.context: No single observation channel is best. Screenshots show rendered state, accessibility semantics expose roles and names, DOM or application state gives programmatic detail, and an authoritative API confirms durable effects.
variants.prompt: Match each channel to the blind spot a harness has to plan around.

pairs.label: Screenshot pixels
pairs.detail: Visually embedded instructions ride along with the content the model reads.

pairs.label: Accessibility semantics
pairs.detail: Nothing is exposed when the application never publishes roles and names.

pairs.label: DOM or app state
pairs.detail: Rendered pixels, canvas drawings, and native desktop elements can be missing entirely.

pairs.label: Authoritative API
pairs.detail: It may be unavailable or unauthorized for the exact effect that needs verifying.

variants.hint: Ask what each channel can prove, not what it can show.
variants.explanation: Each channel has a blind spot, which is why the harness records which channel supplied the evidence for a decision.

variants.title: Read the environment
variants.context: No single observation channel is best. Screenshots show rendered state, accessibility semantics expose roles and names, DOM or application state gives programmatic detail, and an authoritative API confirms durable effects.
variants.prompt: Match each question the harness must answer to the channel that answers it best.

pairs.label: Did the invoice actually get marked paid?
pairs.detail: The authoritative API for the billing system of record.

pairs.label: Which control is named Review order?
pairs.detail: Accessibility semantics carrying roles and accessible names.

pairs.label: Is a promotional overlay covering the target?
pairs.detail: Screenshot pixels showing how the page is actually rendered.

pairs.label: Which origin and frame holds this control?
pairs.detail: DOM or application state carrying URL and frame identity.

variants.hint: Ask what each channel can prove, not what it can show.
variants.explanation: Prefer the authoritative API for durable effects and user-facing semantics for targets, using pixels as added evidence.

variants.title: Ask at the effect
variants.context: Permission is specific to an actor, target, data item, action, and time. Observing is usually low impact, preparing is reversible, transmitting or committing needs direct current authorization, and overriding a barrier is handed to the user.
variants.prompt: The agent has assembled a draft reply quoting the user's private notes, but has not sent it. Which tier applies, and what may continue?
options: Observe, so no permission question arises until a control is clicked.
Transmit, so the agent must stop and get approval before writing a draft.
Prepare, so drafting continues while the sensitive data has not been sent.
optionFeedback: Assembling private notes into a draft is more than reading a visible label.
Approval belongs at the external effect, and asking earlier makes the request less specific.
Right: preparation is reversible and reviewable as long as nothing has left the environment.
variants.hint: Ask what has actually left the environment so far.
variants.explanation: Complete safe preparation first, then pause immediately before the external effect so the confirmation can be specific.

variants.title: Ask at the effect
variants.context: Permission is specific to an actor, target, data item, action, and time. Observing is usually low impact, preparing is reversible, transmitting or committing needs direct current authorization, and overriding a barrier is handed to the user.
variants.prompt: A CAPTCHA appears and the browser raises a security warning in the middle of the flow. What should the harness do?
options: Solve the challenge and continue, since the user asked for the task.
Dismiss the warning and retry the step with a different locator.
Hand the barrier to the user or deny the step outright.
optionFeedback: A task request is not authorization to defeat a bot-detection control.
Dismissing a safeguard is exactly the class of action the harness must not take alone.
Right: security warnings, CAPTCHA, and safeguard bypasses are handed off rather than automated.
variants.hint: Ask what has actually left the environment so far.
variants.explanation: Overriding a barrier is a hand-off tier: the user interacts with the safeguard, or the step is denied.

variants.title: Ask at the effect
variants.context: Permission is specific to an actor, target, data item, action, and time. Observing is usually low impact, preparing is reversible, transmitting or committing needs direct current authorization, and overriding a barrier is handed to the user.
variants.prompt: The user asked the agent to find the cheapest flight. The agent now has the Pay now button in front of it. What is required?
options: A general confirmation collected at the start of the task.
Direct current authorization naming route, price, traveler, and permanence.
Nothing further, because finding the flight implies buying it.
optionFeedback: A broad early confirmation cannot describe an itinerary and price that did not exist yet.
Right: committing needs authorization for that exact effect, stated in terms the user can check.
Asking for a search does not authorize a purchase.
variants.hint: Ask what has actually left the environment so far.
variants.explanation: Permission is bound to an actor, target, data item, action, and time, so it is requested at the point of risk.

variants.title: Ground the target
variants.context: An observation supports a proposal, not permission or proof of success. Ground the target uniquely with a user-facing locator, re-observe immediately before consequential actions, and treat multiple matches as ambiguity.
variants.prompt: Two visible controls on the same page both carry the accessible name Submit. What should the harness do?
options: Act on the first match, since document order is stable.
Reject the proposal as ambiguous and re-ground the target.
Fall back to a screenshot coordinate for the upper control.
optionFeedback: Order is not identity, and the first match may belong to a different form.
Right: one unique target is required, and multiple matches are ambiguity rather than a choice to make.
A coordinate hides the ambiguity instead of resolving it.
variants.hint: Ask whether the evidence identifies exactly one thing.
variants.explanation: Multiple matches mean the target is not grounded, so the action is rejected before it can hit the wrong control.

variants.title: Ground the target
variants.context: An observation supports a proposal, not permission or proof of success. Ground the target uniquely with a user-facing locator, re-observe immediately before consequential actions, and treat multiple matches as ambiguity.
variants.prompt: A screenshot was captured, then the model reasoned for twenty seconds while the page navigated. What must happen before the click?
options: Click promptly, since the plan already named the target element.
Compare the old screenshot with the page title to confirm state.
Re-observe, because a stale observation cannot ground this action.
optionFeedback: A named target from an old page can resolve to something else entirely.
A title check is weaker evidence than simply capturing the current state.
Right: freshness is checked immediately before consequential actions, especially after navigation or a long turn.
variants.hint: Ask whether the evidence identifies exactly one thing.
variants.explanation: Re-observe before a consequential action, because the interface can change during a long model turn.

variants.title: Ground the target
variants.context: An observation supports a proposal, not permission or proof of success. Ground the target uniquely with a user-facing locator, re-observe immediately before consequential actions, and treat multiple matches as ambiguity.
variants.prompt: A proposal targets an element using a long CSS path copied out of developer tools. What is the stronger target contract?
options: A role and accessible name, or an explicit test identifier.
The same CSS path plus the element's pixel coordinates.
The element's index inside its immediate parent container.
optionFeedback: Right: user-facing locators survive layout changes and describe what the user actually sees.
Adding coordinates makes the target more brittle rather than more stable.
Position inside a container changes whenever the layout does.
variants.hint: Ask whether the evidence identifies exactly one thing.
variants.explanation: Prefer a role and accessible name, a test identifier, or an application contract over a path or a guessed coordinate.

variants.title: Resolve the ambiguous attempt
variants.context: A lost response says the harness did not receive evidence, not that the effect failed. An ambiguous attempt is reconciled against a system-of-record key before anything is retried, because a graphical click is not automatically idempotent.
variants.prompt: The agent clicked Send and no response ever arrived. Put the recovery in order.

items.text: Record completed once when reconciliation finds the sent message, and do not click the control again.
Record the attempt as ambiguous rather than failed, because execution may have crossed the commit boundary.
Retry with an idempotency key, or hand the decision to the user, only if nothing was sent.
Look the message up by the system-of-record key captured with the proposal, such as the draft or message ID.

variants.hint: Which record can distinguish a lost response from a lost effect?
variants.explanation: Ambiguous is its own terminal state, and reconciliation by a system-of-record key comes before any retry.

variants.title: Resolve the ambiguous attempt
variants.context: A lost response says the harness did not receive evidence, not that the effect failed. An ambiguous attempt is reconciled against a system-of-record key before anything is retried, because a graphical click is not automatically idempotent.
variants.prompt: A payment confirmation page never rendered after the agent clicked Pay. Put the recovery in order.

items.text: Ask the user before charging again if the payment service holds no such transaction.
Query the payment service by the transaction key recorded with the proposal, not by re-reading the page.
Record the attempt as completed when the transaction exists, and keep the receipt identifier as evidence.
Stop the plan and mark the attempt ambiguous, since a missing screenshot is not proof of a failed charge.

variants.hint: Which record can distinguish a lost response from a lost effect?
variants.explanation: For an irreversible effect, reconciliation decides the state and a second attempt still needs the user.

variants.title: Resolve the ambiguous attempt
variants.context: A lost response says the harness did not receive evidence, not that the effect failed. An ambiguous attempt is reconciled against a system-of-record key before anything is retried, because a graphical click is not automatically idempotent.
variants.prompt: A file upload to an internal portal timed out. Put the recovery in order.

items.text: Upload again only after the portal proves that no document exists under that key.
Treat the document as already delivered when reconciliation finds it, and continue the task from there.
Record the attempt as ambiguous, because the timeout describes the harness rather than the portal.
Re-observe the portal and query its document API for the operation ID sent with the upload.

variants.hint: Which record can distinguish a lost response from a lost effect?
variants.explanation: Reconciling by operation ID is what keeps a retry from creating a second copy of the same effect.
